config.title: Berlin Spy Museum - FAQ
config.subtitle: Straight answers for deciding whether an interactive museum at Potsdamer Platz fits your first Berlin visit.

items.q: Is the Berlin Spy Museum worth visiting?
items.a: It can be worth it when you want an active indoor experience rather than a quiet gallery. The museum’s appeal is the hands-on side, including codes, devices and the laser maze, so it is a better fit for visitors who enjoy taking part. If you mainly want a site-specific account of Berlin history, choose an actual historic location first.

items.q: Where is the German Spy Museum in Berlin?
items.a: The German Spy Museum is at Leipziger Platz, next to the Potsdamer Platz area. That makes it an easy indoor decision during a central Berlin day, but do not visit merely because you are passing through. Decide whether you want an activity-led museum or an outdoor history stop before buying a ticket.

items.q: How long should I allow for the Berlin Spy Museum?
items.a: The museum says it recommends 1.5 to 2 hours for children, which is a sensible signal that this is not a five-minute stop. Your own visit can be shorter or longer, so set a real time boundary and check the current official visitor information before travel.

items.q: Is the Berlin Spy Museum suitable for children?
items.a: The museum recommends its experience from age eight and describes several interactive elements. That is the museum’s own guidance, not a guarantee for every child. Consider your group’s attention span and sensitivity to the subject, then check current visitor information before you go.

items.q: Should I combine the Berlin Spy Museum with Cold War history sites?
items.a: Yes, if you keep the roles clear. The museum can give you an active spy-themed experience, while a real place such as the Berlin Wall Memorial gives a more grounded encounter with the city’s divided past. Do not expect the museum alone to replace a historic site.
